ns2:section.sectionText: TOPIC: Music, Words, and War: England, 1914-1918 This class focuses on the impact of World War I on musical culture in England. We will examine a series of topics, including how composers such as Edward Elgar, Ralph Vaughan Williams, and Arthur Bliss responded to the conflict through their music, both during the war and in its aftermath. Significant time will be spent studying how composers set literary texts (including World War 1 poetry) to music, and we will discuss both art song and popular song, as well as choral repertoire. The reception of such music by contemporary and subsequent generations of writers and composers will form a further strand in the course, as will the way in which music functioned in English culture during the conflict itself. The course will involve reading, listening, paper-writing and class discussion. Students will gain partial credit for attending and participating in an on-campus symposium, 1915: Music, Memory and the Great War (March 2015).
